On a quiet Thursday morning the kitchen light flickers across the worn specks of a coffee mug set on the worn counter. The old radio, perched on the bookshelf, produces a faint static that feels like a memory humming in the back of my mind. When I close my eyes I am taken back to my parents’ house—to the smells of pancakes and fresh‑cut grass in the backyard. Those days were gardens of possibility, where my friend Asher and I would chase each other in the sprinkler’s spray and build a fortress of blankets and laughter in the living room. It was a world that moved slow and still, where stories unfolded at the pace of possibility.

Then comes the current sine‑wave of the world. Shapes of digital lace and endless threads weave through my life. My skull lifts fast with an incessant rush of notifications and hashtags. The beauty of linear time has been swallowed by the urgency of the next “like,” the next “share,” the next stream of content. The organism hurries, losing the sense of raw, of raw wonder that we once found in a sundial. I crave the feeling of simple joy—wandering the old park and watching leaves swirl around the bench. I love the mature feel when a child is in the garden, the scent and colors of a cool oak branch. Where can I find such quiet? My own soul holds that in a restful whisper from within, a light that keeps its own pulse, and in the next quiet moment, I press on, remembering all that lights deep within the heart.
